analysis:
## Technical analysis

### Gate 3 Day 9 — The CPI Catalyst and the $225 Wick

August 12, 2026 is the session that resolved the CPI binary and produced the most technically significant intraday action of Gate 3: a wick to $225.10 — clearing the prior Day 7 high of $225.00 for the first time — with a close at $224.09 ($1.01 fade from the session high). Three weeks of Gate 3 built to this session; what it showed is both encouraging and incomplete.

### Gate 3 Conditions — Day 9, Best Reading of the Cycle

| Condition | Threshold | Day 8 (Aug 11) | Day 9 (Aug 12) | Status |
|-----------|-----------|----------------|----------------|--------|
| (1) NVDA price | > $200 | $217.40 (+$17.40) | $224.09 (+$24.09) | ✓ CLEARED |
| (2) SPX | > 7,460 | 7,728.20 (+$268) | ~7,751 (+$291) | ✓ CLEARED |
| (3) VIX | < 17 | ~14.90 (~2.10 buffer) | ~14.2 (~2.8 buffer) | ✓ CLEARED |

All three conditions are cleared at their widest combined buffers since Gate 3 began July 31. The VIX buffer has improved for three consecutive sessions. The CPI binary — the single most important event of the Gate 3 period — has resolved as constructively as the bull case required.

### The CPI Print — Textbook Bull Scenario

Headline CPI: +0.1% MoM, +3.4% YoY (vs. +3.5% June)  
Core CPI: +0.2% MoM, +2.5% YoY (vs. +2.6% prior)  

Both metrics matched consensus exactly. The September FOMC pause is now the market consensus. The geopolitical risk premium (U.S.-Iran tensions) did not prevent a positive market reaction, though it may cap further near-term upside. NVDA's +3.07% move on CPI day is the direct expression of institutions returning to the stock after Day 8's 42.03M share abstention.

### The $225 Wick — Three-Session Resistance Absorption Sequence

Comparing the three Gate 3 sessions that tested the $225 resistance zone:

| Session | High | Close | Reversal | Reversal % |
|---------|------|-------|----------|------------|
| Day 7 (Aug 10, $500B deal) | $225.00 | $217.54 | $7.46 | 3.4% |
| Day 8 (Aug 11, CPI-eve) | $222.40 | $217.40 | $5.00 | 2.3% |
| Day 9 (Aug 12, CPI day) | $225.10 | $224.09 | $1.01 | 0.45% |

The sellers who drove $7.46 and $5.00 reversals could only manage $1.01 on Day 9. This is the pattern of exhaustion, not strength. The supply overhang at $225 is visibly diminishing session by session. The $1.01 fade is likely the minimum structural level driven by $225 call OI delta hedging — mechanical, not discretionary selling.

### Volume — The Achilles Heel of Day 9

Volume: 57.35M shares = **45% of the 127.49M 30-day average.**

This is the critical technical caveat. A genuine breakout above long-standing resistance on a major catalyst day typically occurs on 150-200% of average volume as the trapped shorts cover and new longs initiate simultaneously. Day 9 produced 57M shares — above Day 8's 42M abstention, but well below average.

What the 57M volume tells us: the Day 9 move was driven by (a) mechanical CPI short covering ($217-$222 shorts buying to cover), (b) $225 call OI delta hedging (sellers of calls buying shares as the strike was approached, then selling as it peaked), and (c) a subset of new institutional longs positioning for the $225 breakout. The institutional accumulation that would signal conviction is not yet present in the volume data.

This is why the close at $224.09 matters: the $225 call sellers absorbed the delta-hedge buying as the strike was approached, then sold it back as NVDA briefly exceeded $225 — mechanical supply at the round number. The next session, with no CPI binary overhang and AI earnings continuing, is when a higher-conviction institutional commitment could push volume above the 130M level and close above $225.

### ★ Strongest Support — $220.20 (Today's Session Low)

Evidence:
1. The CPI gap-up from $217.40 to $220.80 open created a gap zone at $217-$220 that now acts as structural support
2. Buyers stepped in immediately at $220.20 post-open — the session never returned below this level despite the full-session trading
3. The $220 round number creates a double-anchor with the day's technical low
4. Day 9 never gave up the gap-up zone — a bullish sign that institutional buyers defended the $220 level throughout the session

### ★ Strongest Resistance — $225 (Gate 3 Primary Target; Nine-Session Resistance; Call OI Ceiling)

Evidence:
1. Nine consecutive Gate 3 sessions without a single close above $225; the level has been tested intraday twice (Day 7: $225.00, Day 9: $225.10) without a close
2. $225 call OI mechanics: sellers of August $225 calls delta-hedge by selling ~50% of underlying for each call sold when deep-in-the-money; as NVDA approaches $225, the incremental hedging selling creates a mechanical price cap near the strike
3. The $225.10 wick on Day 9 was partially a consequence of this dynamic: the spike above $225 forced call sellers to buy briefly, which pushed the price, before they resumed selling as the gamma exposure peaked
4. Post-Aug 26 earnings, this OI structure will change (August options expire); going into earnings, the $225 and $230 strikes will become the primary near-term call concentration

### AI Earnings Ecosystem — the Underappreciated Day 9 Driver

The CPI is the obvious catalyst. But the AI earnings sector confirmation is equally important:
- CoreWeave (CRWV) +18%: GPU data center utilization rates are high; Blackwell capacity is absorbed
- Super Micro Computer (SMCI) +9%: NVIDIA GPU rack assembly backlog is intact
- Nebius Group +16.5%: global AI infrastructure capex is expanding, not contracting

These results happened on the same day as NVDA's $225 wick. They are not coincidental — they validate the $500B AI financing deal's premise and set the table for NVDA's own Aug 26 earnings. The consensus ($91B guidance, 85% YoY growth) is backed by this supply chain evidence.

### What Confirms vs. What Invalidates

**Confirmed breakout (HIGH conviction upgrade):**
1. Close above $225 with volume >130M shares → resistance absorbed; target $230
2. Gap-open above $225 on continued AI earnings momentum with institutional buy programs
3. Aug 26 earnings beat at >$91B + Jensen Huang quantifies $500B deal margin uplift → 52-week high zone ($235-$236.54)

**Deterioration signals:**
1. Close below $220.20 (today's session low) on above-average volume → gap fill signal; sellers absorbed the CPI bid
2. Geopolitical spike: U.S.-Iran escalation → VIX above 16 → Gate 3 Condition 3 buffer compresses
3. Close below $200 → Gate 3 step-aside formally re-activates
